forces: Release metadata cannot imply publication authority: the governance boundary depends on release artifacts never asserting a releasability nothing here has.

Component tags and per-package manifest entries exist to coordinate publication, and nothing in the repository is publishable: every workspace is private, the SDK is UNLICENSED, and no workflow runs npm publish.
A per-package release model would manufacture the metadata of a publishing repository without the authority to publish, creating a false release story a future reviewer might believe.

The SDK version is pinned by check-coherence.mjs to compatibility.json package.version, so coupling the namespaces would let a documentation commit bump the SDK version while the candidate is unchanged.
The SDK is unpublished, so its version has no external consumer whose expectations coupling would serve; its only consumer is the internal coherence check.
The contract version is owned by the separate security-audit-event-contract governance process under a protected prefix, so no release model may claim or move it.

approach-per-package-component-tags.reason: Component tags and per-package manifest entries exist to coordinate publication, and nothing in this repository is publishable: every workspace is private, the SDK is UNLICENSED, no workflow runs npm publish, and check-publication-path.mjs exists to keep it that way. A per-package model manufactures the metadata of a publishing repository without the authority to publish, and a future reviewer could believe the per-package release story that is not true. It also requires a config change, a tag-collision surface, and per-package restatement of private status, which the repo-scoped model needs none of.

forces: The SDK version is pinned by check-coherence.mjs to compatibility.json package.version, so coupling the namespaces would let a documentation commit bump the SDK version while the candidate is unchanged.
The SDK is unpublished, so its version has no external consumer whose expectations coupling would serve; its only consumer is the internal coherence check.
approach-couple-version-namespaces.reason: Coupling would actively destroy the candidate-identity meaning of the SDK version: the coherence pin exists so the version answers which contract and toolchain the candidate speaks, and a documentation commit would bump it while the candidate is unchanged, turning a meaningful pin into noise. Because the SDK is unpublished, its version has no external consumer whose expectations coupling would serve, so coupling pre-builds a revisit condition for no current benefit.

forces: Per-artifact version ownership must be explicit, so no release or incidental edit can move a package version without a decision.
The contract version is owned by the separate security-audit-event-contract governance process under a protected prefix, so no release model may claim or move it.
approach-implicit-ownership-prose.reason: Prose alone is not a conformance target: RELEASING.md records the ownership table, but nothing gives it normative force, so a future release or incidental edit could move a package version without any gate failing. The issue's acceptance criteria demand that version ownership be explicit, and only a capability requirement with deterministic scenarios makes each artifact's owner and each frozen version an asserted, testable invariant.
